A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IAG study and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–S. Renumbered tables and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V3 reports original attack evaluations, ablations, defense tests, and appendix experiments on transferability, inference time, and real-world examples.

after.justification: V4 retains these empirical results and adds input-only attack comparisons, training-cost measurements, and an absent-target evaluation.

M1.justification: The text-conditioned U-Net, trigger construction, joint training, poisoning procedure, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Loss-symbol corrections clarify the existing objective rather than establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix P adds evaluation with target objects absent from the image, introducing a distinct test condition. All existing dataset and task coverage remains, including COCO-2017, VQA experiments, and real-world examples already present in v3.

E2.justification: New Table 4 substantially broadens comparisons beyond backdoor methods: it evaluates U-Net-only training, a text overlay inside the target box, and PGD across three datasets and two VLMs. Existing comparators remain. U-Net-only training is distinct from the retained trigger-only ablation, which omits the original image.

E3.justification: The added comparisons introduce input-only controls, including PGD with 50 steps, epsilon 8/255, and step size epsilon/50. Table 12 introduces clean-versus-IAG peak-memory and per-iteration timing measurements. Previously reported splits, grounding metrics, poison rates, and training hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds a U-Net-only control examining the need for backdoor training, an absent-target diagnostic in Appendix P, and training-overhead analysis in Appendix L. The existing component ablations, poison-rate study, defense tests, attention visualization, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report inference-time means and standard deviations from 10 sampled questions. V4 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; its new tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: V4 adds substantive comparative and diagnostic results: Table 4 reports input-only attack scores, Table 12 reports training costs, and Appendix P reports accuracy drops exceeding 50 percentage points for absent targets. For example, LLaVA clean/IAG training takes 17.79/20.08 seconds per iteration. Matched pre-existing results remain unchanged; these additions are not improved scores for the original method.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, assumptions A1–A3, and Appendix B's proof and corollaries are unchanged. Equation 3 consistently names the pixel loss Lpix, and Equation 4 explicitly marks the poisoned token history, matching v3's explanation that the history belongs to the respective sequence.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about the first multi-target grounding backdoor, text-conditioned triggers, effectiveness, stealth, robustness, and transferability. New supporting experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix P newly interprets absent-target accuracy drops as semantic manipulation and hallucination contradicting an object-detector explanation. Section 4.2 adds an argument for backdoor access based on input-only comparisons and a robustness comparison with reported Imperio behavior. Appendix L extends the low-overhead interpretation to training.

D1.justification: V4 adds a code URL, input-only attack settings, and concrete training-memory and timing information. The hardware description changes from four NVIDIA RTX6000 48G GPUs to NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPUs, omitting count and capacity. Existing implementation and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds contextual references on VLM applications, backdoors, fingerprinting, and adversarial training, while removing Flamingo. It also removes the assertion that no public VLM backdoor defenses exist and adds an Imperio robustness comparison. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged; several other reference edits merely update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The revision makes local wording, capitalization, notation, bibliography, and cross-reference corrections, adds short explanatory passages, and expands Appendix L's title. The main section sequence and Appendix A–S organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds Tables 4 and 12, renumbers subsequent tables, and adjusts spacing and display placement. Existing figures retain their content; the attention visualization, later case-study figures, and ethics text are relocated. These are limited presentation changes rather than a wholesale redesign.

improvement.justification: The new input-only comparisons and training-cost measurements provide useful evidence for assessing the unchanged method, and the code URL improves access documentation. Gains are limited by the underspecified absent-target experiment and its strong mechanistic interpretation, plus reduced hardware specificity. The revision improves empirical context without substantially changing the paper's established findings.
